author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey handed out $300,000 in relief payments Monday to shellfish harvesters affected by a sewage leak in Haverhill, WHDH reported.

The payments were distributed to eligible harvesters at Woodman’s of Essex. The state’s Division of Marine Fisheries is administering the program, which Healey announced in July after the emergency closure disrupted the start of the summer shellfish season.

Officials said a pressurized sewer line broke in two places near Haverhill’s main pumping station during a June storm, sending millions of gallons of wastewater into the Merrimack River. The leak led to beach closures and a 12-day emergency shellfish closure along parts of the North Shore.
About 130 clammers received checks, according to WHDH. The recipients were from Salisbury, Newburyport, Newbury, Rowley, Ipswich, Essex, Gloucester and Rockport.

The payments are intended to offset lost income during the closure, when many harvesters were working through a high-demand period. The episode also highlighted how a sewer failure upriver can affect coastal businesses and public access to shellfish beds.
dek: Relief checks went to about 130 clammers after a 12-day emergency closure along the North Shore.
headline: Massachusetts shellfish harvesters receive $300,000 after Haverhill sewage leak
